correctness.rationale: Direct edge-intersection signs prove maximum 2m+2 and the exact probability event b<q<a for every generic normal. The azimuth and vertical-coordinate Haar measures are independent and correctly normalized. The integral is evaluated exactly by an arcsine antiderivative. Derivative sign is exactly 1-3cos²(theta)t², proving a unique global optimal height for m>=3. Uniform Taylor expansion yields the sharp pi²/(6sqrt3)m^-2 coefficient. An independent all-edge sign-crossing verifier passes, but finite tests are supplementary, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: For every even regular polygon base of at least six sides, the maximal combinatorial complexity probability has an exact closed law and a unique natural shape optimizing it. The aspect ratio shifts with base complexity and converges to sqrt2, while the best probability decreases with a sharp nontrivial m^-2 rate. This gives meaningful stochastic and geometric design information beyond the already-known cube special case.
